paragraphs.source_en: Nobunaga was no longer the man he had once been. He had subdued the Kinai and Ise, and now possessed the power and majesty proclaimed by his great seal: “Tenka Fubu.” Nor was Hideyoshi the Tōkichirō he had once been. Through several great battles, his outstanding ability and achievements had carried him steadily upward; he now held a fief worth thirty thousand koku in the Imahama region.

paragraphs.source_en: After Ashikaga Yoshiaki was installed as shogun, Nobunaga turned his campaigns toward Ise. He had his second son Nobukatsu inherit the house of Kitabatake Tomonori, governor of Ise, and his third son Nobutaka succeed to the Kanbe house. Having successfully pacified both regions, Nobunaga went to worship at the Great Shrine in Yamada. It was then that he commissioned the “Tenka Fubu” seal.

paragraphs.source_en: Nobunaga’s devotion to the Imperial cause had been influenced by his father Nobuhide, but it also arose from the decay he saw in the world before him. How could such a state of affairs be allowed to continue? Whichever page of history one opened, it was plain to see that the decline of the Imperial House and the decline of the realm were closely bound together. First, the source itself must be set right!
